R1_the_holdback_could_make_no_progress.a_defect_the_first_fix_introduced: the top-up first read THREE bytes, which can carry the whole of the NEXT character's lead -- so `→←↑↓` came back with a replacement character in the middle of it. It reads exactly what is missing now.
R1_the_holdback_could_make_no_progress.and_the_two_endings_are_kept_apart: after the top-up, a still-incomplete tail means the FILE ends mid-character. A LIVE writer may append the rest, so it is held and the follower asks again; a FINISHED writer will not, so it is reported with replacement rather than withheld forever -- terminal malformed data is the writer's, and waiting for it would be the hang this Work removes
R1_the_holdback_could_make_no_progress.correction: the reader TOPS UP a split character instead of withholding it -- a bound is a bound on how much is handed back at once, and reading the bytes that finish a character the caller has already paid for is not a second slice
R1_the_holdback_could_make_no_progress.probe_rerun: the completed euro-sign log at --bound 1 prints €x
R1_the_holdback_could_make_no_progress.what: a completed log holding `€x` followed at --bound 1 withheld the one lead byte it had read, reported bytes_read 0, and the command read that as completion with nothing printed. A live stream would have reread the same prefix forever.
R1_the_holdback_could_make_no_progress.why_my_fix_was_half_right: withholding a split character is correct; withholding it when it is ALL there is makes no progress, and a bound smaller than one character is an ordinary operand rather than an exotic one

absence_vs_inaccessibility.now: ENOENT is the ordinary early tick and stays silent; anything else is a reason the caller declares
absence_vs_inaccessibility.was: _descended collapsed every OSError into None and its caller called that an ordinary not-yet-created directory, so a permission failure or a link where the state directory belongs produced an EMPTY CORNER reported as 'the provider wrote nothing'

restart.now: the resume position is the RETAINED COPY'S OWN SIZE, read from disk. What is already retained is a fact on disk; asking the disk makes restart work by construction rather than by remembering.
restart.was: offsets were per-call-lifetime integers, so a FRESH map over the same durable room appended `abc` a second time -- a restarted capture could not recover its position

truncation_and_replacement.now: the source's (dev, ino) and size are bound to the retained copy. A shorter or different source is a NEW GENERATION with its own retained name and a declared note, so an operator sees two files and an explanation rather than one plausible lie. Neither duplicated nor omitted.
truncation_and_replacement.was: truncating a retained source to `XY` left `abcdef` retained with failed empty -- the new bytes silently omitted
